source.title: Hierarchical supervised contrastive learning with AP-attention encoding for Wi-Fi fingerprinting indoor localization
source.authors: Amr S. Abdelaal; Amr Abdellatif; M. Mahdi

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. Table 6 is flattened and does not show a result for the batch-size 10-to-64 comparison described in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests training-batch effects on held-out localization performance in a new domain, Wi-Fi fingerprinting, rather than the image-classification and language settings named in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out performance for its own architecture and ablations, plus an explicit qualitative statement that increasing fine-tuning batch size from 10 to 64 degrades generalization. It does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, convolutional versus fully connected models, optimizer comparisons, dropout, sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.test_reason: Section 6.2.1 reports worse generalization when fine-tuning batch size increases from 10 to 64 in Wi-Fi localization, bearing qualitatively on V5 in a new setting. No isolated numerical comparison or explicit confirmation of equal epoch budgets accompanies this statement.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that HiSCL-AE improves localization over their reimplemented SAE baseline on UJIIndoorLoc, with multi-seed confirmation, and report baseline deterioration under extended training. They also conclude that learned AP importance alone does not support radio-map compression, and explicitly restrict broader generalization claims because distribution shift and additional datasets were not evaluated.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses labeled Wi-Fi fingerprints and changes the SAE pipeline through a learned AP gate and hierarchical supervised contrastive pre-training; its task, data modality, and method differ from the cited generalization studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports batch-size effects, sensitivity to hierarchical loss weights, poorer performance for an over-tuned schedule, and performance collapse when restricting evaluation to top-K attended APs.

fits_no_version.finding: HiSCL-AE improves held-out localization over the reimplemented SAE baseline, including across ten seeds; individual components also improve the single-seed headline metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AP gating and hierarchical supervised contrastive pre-training can improve SAE-based localization on UJIIndoorLoc.

fits_no_version.finding: The jointly altered pre-training schedule performs worse than the default schedule.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: HiSCL-AE localization performance depends on its combined pre-training configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Retaining only highly weighted APs severely worsens localization because importance ranking does not ensure spatial coverage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Global AP attention rankings alone do not preserve localization performance under input-feature reduction.

record.problems: Experiments use only UJIIndoorLoc. The 10-to-64 fine-tuning batch-size result is qualitative in the text and has no visible numeric result. The over-tuned configuration comparison changes multiple settings, and Table 6 is flattened. State-of-the-art method comparisons use a single seed; the paper notes multi-seed significance analysis across those methods is future work.
record.rows_left_out: No reported table results omitted. The Table 7 loss-weight sensitivity results are not listed as separate rows because they vary a training hyperparameter outside the claim versions. The Table 11 method comparisons are likewise outside the mapped versions and use adapted reimplementations; the paper states the original methods were evaluated under this study's protocol.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width scaling beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization on images and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons and tuning-dependent differences.

Image and language benchmarks; explicit verification of matched epoch budgets in the 10-to-64 comparison; batch thresholds; recovery through longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization or regularization changes.
Controlled dropout comparisons, dataset-size dependence and joint removal of dropout and weight decay. Table 12's convergence-related dropout adaptation does not measure held-out benefits.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. V5 support rests on an explicit qualitative finding, not Table 6's confounded schedule comparison. Missing numerical outcomes are an evidence limitation, not an omitted reported result. States for rows linked to none indicate that those measures cannot establish a listed claim's effect.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and natural-label generalization coexistence.

Image-classification and language benchmarks; workload-dependent batch thresholds; the effects of longer training, warmup, learning-rate scaling, normalization, or regularization adaptations. The 10-to-64 fine-tuning batch comparison has no displayed numeric result.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
